title: The Last Gravity
premise: Silas Thornbury, a clone haunted by the original's unsolved murder, is conscripted to investigate the Meridian, a deep-space vessel whose crew returned biologically younger and with no memory of their voyage. As Silas digs, he discovers the crew traded their years—and their memories of a massacre at the colony Vesper Gate—to a corporate entity called Continuum for passage home, while every official record of the colony has been rewritten. Pursued by Continuum's enforcers and betrayed by an ally, Silas recovers the erased truth from his own original's hidden logs: the murder he inherited was the first attempt to expose the same atrocity. In the end, Silas broadcasts the massacre record at the cost of his own ship and freedom, choosing truth over survival and finally making peace with the man he was cloned from.
about_author: Ivo Montrose is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal city and write about people who carry other people's debts.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Silas Thornbury hauls contraband ice through contested orbits, dodging toll collectors and memories that aren't technically his. A routine salvage call brings him alongside the Meridian, drifting silent. POV Silas. Beat: weary competence masking a hollow core.

chapters.title: The Younger Crew
chapters.summary: Aboard the Meridian, Silas finds thirty crew members biologically twenty years younger than their service records, healthy and serene—and unable to describe their voyage. One woman, Dr. Ansel, flinches when he says 'Vesper Gate.' POV Silas. Beat: uncanny dread beneath calm surfaces.

chapters.title: Inherited Ghosts
chapters.summary: Station authorities detain Silas, noting his clone registry and the original Thornbury's open murder case. Investigator Rhee Okafor offers him a deal: consult on the Meridian or lose his shipping license. POV Silas. Beat: resentment at being owned by another man's life.

chapters.title: Records That Lie
chapters.summary: Silas cross-references flight manifests and finds Vesper Gate colony—population eleven thousand—officially never existed. Port archives show seamless, impossible edits. Someone with systemic access rewrote history. POV Silas. Beat: cold realization the cover-up is institutional.

chapters.title: Ansel's Silence
chapters.summary: Dr. Mara Ansel privately tells Silas she dreams in a child's handwriting she can't read. She begs him to stop asking questions, terrified of what remembering will cost her. POV Ansel. Beat: sympathy entangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: Continuum
chapters.summary: A polished corporate liaison, Wren Castile, visits Silas with an offer: generous pay to close the inquiry as equipment malfunction. He mentions the original Thornbury by name—and how he died asking similar questions. POV Silas. Beat: temptation sharpened into threat.

chapters.title: The Murder File
chapters.summary: Silas opens the original's case file for the first time: photos, a half-decoded cipher, a note reading 'they sold the years.' The murder scene matches Continuum methodology. His inheritance becomes a lead. POV Silas. Beat: reluctant kinship with the dead man.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Cargo
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in the original Thornbury's voice, reconstructed from logs: hauling refugees from Vesper Gate, witnessing the evacuation that wasn't, hiding data in a freight manifest. POV Original Silas. Beat: the past pressing its weight onto the present.

chapters.title: Okafor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Rhee Okafor reveals her own file was edited—she served at Vesper Gate and remembers nothing. She chooses to help Silas off the books. POV Okafor. Beat: two broken people building fragile trust.

chapters.title: The Cipher Breaks
chapters.summary: Using the Meridian's anomalous aging as a key, Silas cracks the original's cipher: coordinates, dates, and a passenger list of eleven thousand names marked 'expended.' POV Silas. Beat: grief arriving as arithmetic.

chapters.title: What the Crew Bought
chapters.summary: Ansel confesses under sedation-adjacent honesty: Continuum offered the crew youth and memory-wipe in exchange for silence about the colony's destruction—their ship carried the weapon. POV Ansel. Beat: horror at what survival purchased.

chapters.title: Tailspin
chapters.summary: Continuum moves: Okafor is suspended, Silas's ship impounded, Ansel transferred to a 'medical facility.' The machinery of erasure turns toward them. POV Silas. Beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: The Black Yard
chapters.summary: Silas breaks into a decommissioned shipyard where Continuum stores physical backups—paper, tape, things that can't be edited remotely. He finds the Vesper Gate master ledger. POV Silas. Beat: desperate courage.

chapters.title: Betrayal
chapters.summary: Okafor delivers Silas to Castile—her reinstatement was the price. But she slips him a storage chip mid-arrest, whispering that some debts can't be paid twice. POV Okafor. Beat: betrayal braided with sacrifice.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Castile offers Silas Continuum's true prize: a fresh original body, a new life, the murder case closed forever. Silas realizes they fear him because clones can't be fully memory-edited without collapsing. POV Silas. Beat: understanding why he, specifically, matters.

chapters.title: Escape Velocity
chapters.summary: Silas escapes custody during a station-wide power diversion he sabotaged from inside, reclaiming his ship from impound with Ansel smuggled aboard as cargo. POV Silas. Beat: kinetic release after suffocation.

chapters.title: Vesper Gate
chapters.summary: They jump to the colony's coordinates and find only a debris field and a still-functioning memorial beacon the killers missed—broadcasting names on loop for twenty years. POV Ansel. Beat: mourning made physical.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ansel chooses partial restoration: she takes back enough memory to testify, knowing it will age her decades and may kill her. 'I bought my life with theirs,' she says. POV Ansel. Beat: costly reclamation of self.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Silas hijacks the station's public relay to transmit the ledger, the crew testimony, and the original's logs. Continuum ships converge; Okafor, redeeming herself, holds the legal channel open. POV Silas. Beat: the climax—truth versus force.

chapters.title: Collision
chapters.summary: The Meridian's sister ship rams Silas's freighter as the broadcast completes. Silas rides the wreck down toward the station, the data already propagating beyond anyone's reach. POV Silas. Beat: sacrifice with no guarantee.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: The massacre record goes public; Continuum fractures, executives flee, inquiries begin. Okafor reopens the original Thornbury's murder case—and closes it, naming his killers. POV Okafor. Beat: justice as accounting, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Last Gravity
chapters.summary: Injured but alive, Silas drifts in a hospital ward, finally able to say 'my name' without irony. Ansel, aged and at peace, visits. Memory, he decides, is the last gravity—what everything falls back toward. POV Silas. Beat: quiet resolution and earned identity.
